relations.subject: sgw:secure-administration
relations.evidence: Sync Gateway 4.1.0 brings additional optional but default layers of security through [enforcing TLS encryption](../security/secure-sgw-access.md) for all API traffic and Couchbase Server Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) authorization and authentication for all [Admin and Metrics API users](#lbl-secure-users).

relations.subject: sgw:secure-administration
relations.evidence: RBAC user authentication enables [Secure Administration](#lbl-secure-users) of Sync Gateway clusters.

relations.object: api.admin_interface_authentication and api.metrics_interface_authentication bootstrap settings, or -admin_interface_authentication=false / -metrics_interface_authentication=false CLI flags
relations.evidence: You can choose to disable Secure Administration by using these bootstrap configuration settings or CLI flags:

relations.subject: sgw:admin-rest-api
relations.evidence: Admin port. Internal HTTP port for unrestricted access to the database and to run administrative tasks. The Admin REST API is used to administer user accounts and roles. It can also be used to look at the contents of databases in superuser mode. The default port for the Admin REST API is 4985\.

relations.subject: sgw:admin-rest-api
relations.object: bound to 127.0.0.1 (loopback interface), unreachable from any other host
relations.evidence: As a useful special case, the IP address 127.0.0.1 binds to the loopback interface, making the port unreachable from any other host. This is the default setting for the admin interface.

relations.subject: sgw:public-rest-api
relations.evidence: Public port. External HTTP port used for replication with Couchbase Lite databases and other applications accessing the REST API on the Internet. The Public REST API is used for client replication. The default port for the Public REST API is 4984.

notable_absence.finding: Table 1's 6.1-7.0 column and Table 2's endpoint-role names (in rest-api-access-rbac-roles.md) use inconsistent labels for what appear to be the same handful of legacy roles: this page has 'Application Access' AND 'Bucket Full Access' as two separate rows (matching the registry's already-recorded old-name/new-name pair for role:bucket-full-access), while 'Sync-Gateway Role' here (hyphenated) becomes 'Sync Gateway Role' (no hyphen) in rest-api-access-rbac-roles.md, and that page additionally uses a fourth label, 'Bucket Application Access', not seen on this page at all and not confidently mergeable with either 'Application Access' or 'Bucket Admin' without more evidence - flagged rather than force-merged per this round's instructions.

cross_component_finding: This page names the actual Server RBAC role catalogue Sync Gateway introduces for its own Admin/Metrics API use (Sync Gateway Architect/Application/Application Read Only/Replicator/Dev Ops, plus the legacy Sync-Gateway Role) - none of which are in the generic 56-role Server catalogue excerpt this batch was given, confirming these are Sync-Gateway-specific additions to Couchbase Server's RBAC system rather than reuses of pre-existing generic roles (aside from Full Admin / Application Access / Bucket Full Access, which clearly are the generic roles).
cross_product_finding: The explicit 'This user cannot read application data' carve-outs on both Sync Gateway Architect and Sync Gateway Replicator show Couchbase deliberately keeping the Admin-API's Server-RBAC layer separate in EFFECT, not just in identity, from the channel-based read access sgw:read-access-control governs - an operations/administration role on the Admin REST API side grants no implicit visibility into application documents, which still requires a channel grant in the entirely separate sgw:user/sgw:channel system. This is a concrete instance of round 27's 'no relationship' finding actually holding at the level of what each system's roles/grants let you SEE, not just at the level of stated intent.
